justification: B puts the title in a strong navy band on the first page, so the document opens as a single unit. Its body text is one consistent size and indent, and the running header and footer are clear (B1, B2). A uses a nearly empty title page (A1), and its body text and indents vary: drop caps, inconsistent paragraph sizes and different left margins in Abstract, Introduction and Methods (A2, A3). B's table is clean and the page count is leaner, though B's formula splits from its lead-in sentence across pages and its last page is mostly empty. A's drop caps add some character but make the rhythm uneven.

A has a strong navy title band, clear section rules, a bold sans-serif hierarchy, running headers and footers, and a styled table. B is a plain serif document with numbered headings and no visual anchor. Both leave page 3 mostly empty and both show the raw '$s_p$' glitch. A splits the formula from its lead-in sentence across pages, and B does the same. A's section rules keep its rhythm clearer.

A has a calm navy header band and a serif heading hierarchy. Its table fits the margins cleanly, and its Region column stays on fewer lines than B's (A1). B's saturated blue band is heavier. The sans heading clashes with the serif body, and the indented body and table sit awkwardly against the rule and heading edges (B1). B's narrower Region column wraps more, which makes rows taller. A repeats a top rule on continuation pages, but B has a similar repeat (A2, B2). B fits more rows per page but looks more cramped (B2).

A keeps a consistent text column, numbered headings and steady spacing, with a clean running header and footer. B has inconsistent body text sizes and indents (Participants larger than Procedure), awkward drop caps that leave ragged lines, and heavy rules between every section. B's headings also hang out into the left margin while its body is indented. B's table is acceptable but sits tighter in a cramped layout. A's last page is mostly empty, but B's final page is too.

A has a dark navy title band, numbered section headings and navy header/footer bands that give a clear, consistent frame on every page (A1, A2, A3). Its table is aligned to the same margins as the headings. B's table and body text are indented relative to the heading, which breaks the left edge (B1). B's status column wraps 'Ahead of' awkwardly, and its plain footer is weaker. B does fit one more row per page and has a lighter feel, but A looks more polished and gives a stronger hierarchy.

Design B pairs a serif with a clear accent rule and has a pulled quote that works as a real hierarchy element (B3). Its text sits in a column beside the image, so pages feel composed (B2, B4), and the cover is calm and elegant (B1). Design A has a nicer illustrated cover (A1), but its last page holds only a small image at the top left and is otherwise empty (A4). Its text wraps awkwardly around the figure on page 2, leaving an orphaned line (A2), and its running header and footer bands are heavy.

Design B holds together better. Its elegant serif type, consistent running header, overlay quote boxes and pull quote give a coherent editorial feel, and its last page keeps the image with the section text. Design A has a stronger illustrated cover, but its final page is almost empty. That page holds only an orphaned image, separated from its section text, and the layout reads as broken (A4). A's heavy header and footer bands are also busier. B's plain cover is less striking, and its page 3 ends with a large empty area, but these are minor next to A's flaws.

A has clear numbered sans-serif headings with a serif body, a running header showing the current section, and a consistent text size. B's headings are light and weak, with heavy rules between every section. B also mixes body sizes (the Participants paragraph is larger than the others), and its references split across pages, leaving the last page nearly empty. B's dark cover is bold but its text sits low, while A's cover is simple and centred. A's last page is mostly empty with only footnotes, but that is a smaller flaw.

B uses a clean sans-serif with tabular figures that are easy to scan. Its header and footer bands give each page clear navigation (B2, B3), and its row dividers are lighter. B also fits more rows per page, so the third page is lighter than A's. A has an elegant serif and a heavier title band, but its figures are smaller and its rules are heavier. Its page 3 has a lot of empty space, and its footer is faint (A2, A3).

A uses one sans family, and its navy title band plus header and footer bands on pages 2 and 3 frame the document consistently. Its table columns are clean, and its "Region" cells wrap less (A1, A2). B mixes a serif body with a bold sans heading and has no running header or footer bands. Its narrow Region column wraps more, making rows taller, and the indented text sits oddly against the left-aligned rule (B1, B2). B does fit more rows per page and avoids an almost empty page 3, but A looks more polished.

A keeps each section together with a consistent serif voice, a coral rule and a header band. Each image sits with its text, so pages 2-4 look cohesive. B has an orphaned image at the top of B3 that is detached from its section, and a stray paragraph at the top of B4 that continues from the previous page. B's headings are left-hung against indented body text, which looks misaligned, and its margins are inconsistent. A's page 4 leaves a large empty area, but B's page 4 has the same problem.

B has an illustrated cover and consistent header and footer bands. Its pull quotes sit beside the images (B2, B3), and its body text keeps a coherent left edge. A's cover is a dark empty page (A1). Its text is indented inconsistently and mixes sizes (A2). Its image is orphaned at the top of A3, and A4 is half empty with an awkward layout. B has flaws too: B4 is an orphaned image on a mostly blank page, and B2 has a text wrap break. Overall B is more polished and consistent.

B is more cohesive and refined: an elegant serif, gold rules that mark sections consistently, a full-width hero image, a pull-quote with real presence, and the text overlay on the flower image (B3). Its cover is plain but classy. A has a stronger cover image (A1), but its body pages are cramped, with a narrow image, a small quote and a bare number-run caption. The A3 text block abuts the flower image awkwardly, and the caption is orphaned onto A4. B also splits a caption (B3) and hyphenates 'vo-lunteer' (B4). Both have empty space at the bottom of the last page. A's heavy teal bands (A2 to A4) are consistent but busier.

Both designs use near-identical tables that repeat the header row on each page. B keeps the content flush with the table edge and wraps 'Ahead of plan' cleanly onto two lines, which makes the Status column easier to scan (B1, B2). A indents the intro text but not the table, and its Status column is tighter against the Week column (A1). B's running header and footer bands on pages 2-3 add navigation and consistency, and the dark navy header is more refined than A's bright blue. A's footers are lighter and the page 3 notes are fine, but A has no running header. B's numbered headings add structure. B also fits fewer rows on page 2, which leaves a larger gap at the page bottom and makes its page 2 less full than A's.

A uses a refined serif throughout and an elegant, quiet cover with a short accent rule. Its pull quote sits as a card over the image, and the page 3 statement works as a real pull quote. Page 4 is sparse, but the image sits beside its text. B has a more illustrative cover and clear running header and footer bands. But its numbered sans headings feel generic, and its pull quote is small and weak. Page 4 is left with an orphaned image and a vast empty page, which is the worst flaw in either design. A's page 4 is also sparse but better composed.

A has an illustrated cover and running header and footer bands. Its numbered headings are consistent, and the pull-quote panels sit cleanly beside the images (A2, A3). Its flaw is the last page (A4), which holds only an orphaned image with a mostly empty page. B has a bare, empty cover. Its headings hang out in the left margin while body text is indented, and its text sizes vary within paragraphs. Its pull quote is stranded at the page bottom, and the figure at the top of B3 is separated from its text. Overall B is less coherent, though B4 is better balanced than A4.

A uses a clean sans-serif throughout. Its columns are tighter, and the Region column is wide enough that most region names fit on fewer lines (A1). Its light heading with a rule above it reads cleanly. B's serif body with a bold numbered heading is acceptable, but its Region and Status columns wrap more, so rows are taller (B1-B2). B's hyphen-minus signs on negatives look weaker than A's true minus signs. The header and footer bands are essentially the same in both. A's table rows are more compact and consistent.

Design A has a striking dark cover (A1) and elegant serif headings with rules (A2, A3). But the body text size varies inconsistently: the Abstract and Participants paragraphs on A2 are larger than the Introduction. Rules above every section make the pages feel choppy, and the references split across pages leaving A4 nearly empty. Design B uses numbered sans headings over a serif body, a consistent body size, a running header and a compact booktabs-style table (B3). Its page flow is tidier, with all references on one page. Its cover is plainer, and the footnotes alone on B4 leave a mostly empty page. Overall B is more consistent and readable.

A uses an elegant serif with clear heading hierarchy, a restrained accent rule, and a pull quote set as a large statement (A3). Body text and images sit comfortably together, and the cover is minimal but refined (A1). B has a stronger cover image (B1) and heavy header and footer bands. B's page 2 has an awkward text wrap that leaves a paragraph hanging beneath the image. B's page 4 is a lone image with an empty page, and its pull quote is weak (B3). A's page 4 is also sparse but the text and image are paired.

A opens with a compact header band and puts content straight onto page 1, with a fuller, more economical flow over 3 pages. B spends a whole page on a cover that repeats the hero image on page 2. B also strands the photo caption at the top of page 4, away from its image on page 3, and leaves the stat row hanging with empty space below on page 2. A's caption also sits slightly below its image, but the pairing holds better. A's lighter headings with orange rules give clearer section rhythm, while B's numbered bold headings are fine but the layout is looser. Both leave empty space at the bottom of the last page.

B adds a dark navy cover page (B1) and rules above each section with running footers (B2, B3), which makes it look more finished. A has bold numbered headings with clear hierarchy, but it is plain and has no cover or running footer (A1, A2). B's section headings are light-weight and a little inconsistent with the paragraph sizes: some body paragraphs, such as Participants, are larger than others (B2). Both leave a mostly empty final page and both show the unrendered $s_p$ glitch (A2, B2). B's cover and section rules give it the stronger overall impression, though the size inconsistency keeps the margin modest.

A has an elegant serif cover and a pull quote set as a clear display element (A2). Its stat row sits right under the 'What changed' intro, and the callout is overlaid on the image (A3). B splits the stats from their intro, leaving a gap at the bottom of page 1, and its quote is small and weak (B1). B's header and footer bands are heavy but consistent (B2, B3). B's cover is combined with content, so it has less presence. Both tables are similar and clean.

A pairs a bold sans heading with a serif body, so numbered section headings (A1, A3) stand out clearly. B's light-weight headings 'Pipeline by Region' and 'Notes' are weak against the table (B1, B3). A's table has a stronger header rule, and its closing rule and tighter columns make it a little easier to scan. B wraps 'Ahead of plan' similarly, but its 'Latin America' fits on one line, which is a small plus. Overall A has the clearer hierarchy and more polished type.

A opens with a strong navy title band and puts the content on the first page, so it looks finished and reads efficiently. Rules between sections give a clear rhythm, and the 3-page length is tighter. However, A splits the formula from its sentence across a page break and leaves the final page mostly empty. B has a mostly blank cover page and a near-empty last page holding only footnotes. B's numbered sections and serif body are clean and consistent, but its look is plainer and has no band.

A sets body text in a serif face, justified, with numbered headings that make the sections easy to follow. Its paragraphs flow cleanly around the floated image on A2. B has a sans body that is widely spaced, and on B2 the text wraps awkwardly beside the image, with the line 'one oven, one van...' stranded below it. Both leave page 4 nearly empty apart from one image, and A also has some hyphenation and a wide gap at the bottom of A2. A's caption on A4 wraps into an orphan, which is a small flaw.

A has a bold blue title band and bold sans section headings (Pipeline by Region, Notes), so hierarchy is clearer. Its table header uses blue rules and fits more rows per page (11 and 15 versus 10 and 13). B has a restrained dark band and light headings that are less distinct. It repeats a heavy rule at the top of continuation pages, which adds clutter. Both tables are similar in readability, but A's wrapped region names take more vertical space.

A has a dark cover page with a strong title, a running header rule, footers, and rules separating sections, so it looks more polished and the hierarchy is clearer. Its body text sizes are inconsistent: the Abstract and Participants paragraphs are larger than the others. B is a plain, consistent Times-style layout with numbered headings, but it looks generic. Both share the same defects: the unrendered $s_p$ and an orphaned reference page. B's formula is split from its explanation across a page break.

Design A has a stronger navy title band and running header and footer bands with page numbers on pages 2 and 3. Its sans-serif table is crisp and easy to scan, and it fits 11 rows on page 1 and 14 on page 2. Design B uses a serif face that is lighter and smaller in the table, a plain thin rule instead of a header band, and a bare footer. Its rows are comparable, but it looks less structured and has less emphasis.

B uses a serif face with a full-bleed cover and a large pull quote, and its callout sits over the image in a polished way. Its tables and chart are clean. A has a strong header band and a tidy side-by-side callout, but its justified text shows rivers and hyphenation, the quote is tiny, and the stat row is separated from the 'What changed' text it belongs to. A also ends page 1 with a large empty gap and page 3 with a very empty lower half. B has a similar empty last page but a more coherent editorial feel. The scores lean towards A on several criteria, but the overall preference is B, so the sign convention is inconsistent.

A uses rules between sections, drop caps and a Montserrat/serif pairing. Its hierarchy is clearer, the cover title is left-aligned on a rule, and the layout feels more designed (A1, A2, A3). Its indentation is inconsistent, with mixed body sizes and a short last page. B is clean and consistent, with numbered headings and running headers. Its justified text has hyphenation like 'university-e-ducated' and loose spacing, and its last page holds only footnotes (B3, B4). B is plainer but more even to read.

A has a dark full-bleed cover band and a consistent serif system with aligned headings, rules and a top band on each page. B's sans headings are bold and clear, but its section headings sit out in the margin while the body is indented, which looks misaligned. B's drop caps are awkward and its body text varies in size, with the Abstract and Participants paragraphs larger than the others. B also has a running footer that wrongly says 'Participants' on page 2. A is more cohesive, though its body text also varies in size.

Design B is more consistent. It has a full cover page, a steady heading style, amber rules, a running header and the same margins throughout. Its pull quote and stat row sit well together on B2, and the chart on B3 is large with a cohesive navy palette. Design A has a stronger masthead band and a full-bleed image, but it leaves large empty areas: A1 ends with a blank lower third, A2 has a big gap under the chart, and A4 holds only two lines of text. A also mixes indents and left-aligned heading styles, and its justified text shows wide gaps. The chart colour in A is black and does not match the palette.

A's cover uses the illustration with a title block. Its running header and footer bands are consistent, and its callouts are paired cleanly with images (A2, A3). Its flaws are a stranded final page with one image (A4) and body text wrapping awkwardly under the figure on A2. B's cover is an empty dark page. B has inconsistent indents, with headings flush left and body indented. The Shed four image is orphaned at the top of B3 and separated from its section. The pull quote is split from its paragraph and the text splits across pages (B3, B4). B's large empty areas at the bottom of B2 and B4 add to the unbalanced feel.

A opens with a strong navy title band and a compact title block, so the first page carries content. Its sans headings and justified body are consistent, and the running headers and footers are tidy. B spends a whole page on a mostly empty cover. B's body text shifts between sizes and indents (the Participants paragraph is larger than the Procedure text). Its drop caps are inconsistent, with the Introduction one misaligned with the text beside it. Its left-hung headings with indented body leave a ragged left edge. A's flaws are the equation split across pages and the stray $s_p$ markup, which B shares.

B has an illustrated cover and consistent header and footer bands. Its numbered headings and callouts sit cleanly beside the images (B2, B3). A's cover is a plain dark page with a lot of empty space (A1). A's image sits alone at the top of A3, away from its text. A4 leaves half the page empty and has inconsistent body sizes. B4 is a stranded image on an otherwise blank page, which is a real flaw. Even so, B is more polished overall.

A has a dedicated cover page with an accent rule, bold sans headings against a serif body, running headers and footers, and a clear heading hierarchy (A2, A3). Its table is cleaner with a stronger rule and tighter structure (A3). A's last page holds only two footnotes, which is wasteful (A4). B is a plain Word-like document in Times with weaker heading contrast, and its references split across pages. Footnotes there trail the references, and the page 3 is mostly empty (B2, B3). B's text is denser but looks generic.

A has a full-bleed cover with a teal band, consistent header and footer bands, numbered headings and teal accents that make a cohesive, polished report (A1-A4). Its caption sits at the foot of the page, though, and the stat row and chart are separated. B has a weak cover that is merged into page 1, with a large empty area below the image (B1). Its heading and body indents are misaligned, the black chart is heavy, the caption sits far from its image, and the last page holds almost nothing (B4). B's overlay quote card on the image is nice, and its table is clean (B3).

A has a full-bleed cover with a restrained palette. Its margins are consistent and its headings, rules and running header are coherent (A2, A3). The chart and image sit well within the text column, and the teal chart ties in with the cover colour. B's headings hang left of an indented body, which looks misaligned. B's full-bleed image cuts into the text (B1), the black chart is harsh against the teal, and B4 is nearly empty. B's table is fine, but A's is equally clean.

B has a full-bleed cover with a teal band, consistent running header and footer bands, and numbered headings, which makes it feel like one coherent report. Its teal chart and stat figures match the palette, and the table has teal rules. A is cohesive in places, but page 4 is nearly empty with one short paragraph, and the stat row and chart are split from the caption area. The black bars in A's chart clash with the teal palette. B has flaws too: the chart is separated from its section, the image caption is orphaned onto page 4, and there is slack space on pages 2 and 4. A's whitespace is worse, with a large gap at the bottom of page 1 and an almost blank page 4.

B keeps a consistent system: a running header band, a uniform serif, and images that sit beside their text (B2, B4). Its sections stay together, and the pull quote and the closing paragraph flow in order (B3). A has bolder sans headings, but its layout breaks apart. The Shed four image is orphaned at the top of A3, separated from the 'people of the quay' text on A2. The pull quote is stranded at the bottom of A3, with its following paragraph pushed to A4. Heading sizes are inconsistent (A2 vs A3), and A4 leaves a large empty lower half. B also has an empty lower half on B4, but the rest of its flow is cleaner.

A pairs a bold geometric sans for headings with a serif body, so Abstract, Introduction and Methods stand out clearly (A2). The drop caps and indented body give a more editorial feel. B sets its section headings in light serif at nearly body weight, which weakens the hierarchy (B2, B3). B's dark cover band is striking, but its accent rule is nearly invisible against the dark ground (B1). Both designs end with a mostly empty final page. A's running footer carries section names, which helps; B repeats the document title.

B's sans-serif table sits wider with fewer wrapped lines ("Latin America" stays on one line), and its rows are tighter and more regular. Its running header and footer bands (B2, B3) frame the pages and aid navigation. A has a bolder, more distinct heading hierarchy (A1) and a serif body that looks elegant, but its narrower columns wrap more and its table is indented. A's last page also carries only four rows plus notes, and its footer is plain. B's section heading is lighter in weight, which weakens its hierarchy slightly.

B has a navy title band, thin rules between sections, bold sans subheads, and running headers and footers, so it reads as a polished, scannable document (B1, B2). A is a plain serif default layout with an unnumbered first page and no page furniture, which looks generic (A1, A2). B's table is cleaner, with a stronger header rule and consistent spacing (B2). Both leave page 3 mostly empty, and both show the raw '$s_p$' text. B's light-weight section headings are a little weak, but overall it is more refined.

B repeats its navy header and footer bands on pages 2 and 3, which gives continuity and running context (B2, B3). Its table is denser with more rows per page, and the Status column wraps more cleanly as 'Ahead / of plan'. Its bold sans headings with numbering give a stronger hierarchy than A's light serif headings. A's table is also readable, but its first page has more empty space at the bottom and its later pages have only a thin top rule and a small footer (A2, A3). A's lighter rules are elegant, but its 'Ahead of' wrapping is less tidy.

B runs three pages with a consistent header and footer band, accent rules and a teal-matched chart and callout. Its content flows without large dead gaps. A spreads over four pages, and page 4 holds only two lines under a large empty area. A's page 2 also has a big blank lower half. A's full-bleed image is striking, and its heavy headings and black chart are strong, but the pagination is wasteful. B's chart and callout colours fit the palette better, though its quote is small and weak and its section headings are light.

A is a compact, consistent academic layout with a clear serif heading hierarchy and uniform body text. B adds a mostly empty cover page, and its rules and drop caps are decorative but inconsistent. B's indents are uneven and body text size varies: Participants is larger than Procedure, and the drop-cap paragraphs are ragged. Running headers such as 'Participants' are mismatched, and B's table and heading rules are fine but add clutter. B also splits the references across two pages and leaves a final page mostly empty. A's last page is also mostly empty, but it is shorter overall.

Both share the same cover and a nearly empty final page with an orphaned image. Design A has a sans-serif body, and its page 2 text wraps around the figure so that a paragraph breaks off beneath it (A2). B uses a serif body with numbered headings, which gives clearer hierarchy. B's page 2 keeps the figure beside its paragraphs, but the smokehouse paragraph spills onto page 3 (B2, B3). B's page 3 is fuller and more evenly balanced, while A's page 3 leaves a large empty bottom (A3). B's serif body and numbered headings read more cleanly, but the orphaned paragraph and the caption wrapping on B4 are small flaws. Overall it is close.

A has a refined serif type system, thin amber rules between sections, and a pull quote set large as a real accent. The caption stays with its image (A3), and the text sits in a callout over the image. B's cover is strong, but its pages carry heavy header and footer bands. B's numbered bold sans headings feel generic, and its quote is small and weak. B's image caption is orphaned onto the next page (B4), and the callout beside the image is cramped. A's cover is plain but elegant. A's bottom-of-page gaps are similar to B's.

A opens with a strong title band, so the first page is useful and the title and abstract sit together. Its sans-serif body and bold subheads are clear and consistent, and its running header bands aid navigation. B spends page 1 on a mostly empty dark cover, which pushes the content to four pages. B's Participants paragraph is set larger than the other body text, which breaks the rhythm. A does split the formula from its lead-in sentence across pages 1 and 2, and both designs leave a nearly empty last page and show the raw '$s_p$'.

A pairs a serif body with bold numbered headings, which gives a clear hierarchy and comfortable reading (A2, A3). Its cover page is sparse but elegant. Its last page holds only two footnotes and is mostly empty (A4). B has a strong navy title band (B1), but its thin light section headings are weak against the body text, and the many rules are repetitive. B also splits the formula from its lead-in across pages (B1 to B2) and splits the reference list across pages (B2 to B3). The tables are similar in both designs.

A has a bold sans-serif title and numbered headings that are clearly stronger than B's light headings. Its navy running header and footer bands frame the pages and show the section and page number. Its table rows are tidy, and the region names wrap cleanly. B's table is clean and slightly more compact, but its headings are thin and weak, and its footer is minimal. B also wraps 'Ahead of / plan' awkwardly, and its thin top rule on pages 2-3 is less useful than A's header bands.

A has a distinct cover page, a sans-serif heading and serif body pairing, blue rules between sections and drop caps, so the hierarchy is clear and the page looks designed (A1, A2, A3). Its indentation and font sizes vary between paragraphs, and the page 4 tail is mostly empty. B is a plain default Times layout with no rules or accent colour, and its heading hierarchy is weaker, although it is consistent and compact (B1, B2). In B the table and the formula are handled much as in A, and both leave a stray unrendered $s_p$. Overall A is more polished.

A is cohesive: teal header band, matching teal stat rules, teal chart bars and running header/footer bands, and consistent margins across 3 pages (A1-A3). B has misaligned heading and body indents, a full-bleed image that clashes with the margins, black chart bars, a quote stranded at the top of page 2, a dark box overlapping the image, and a nearly empty fourth page with one short section (B1-B4). A's last page also has a lot of empty space, but B's is worse.

B pairs a sans-serif heading face with a serif body, gives numbered headings clear weight, adds running headers and footers, and sets a booktabs-style table with a rule above and below. Its reference list is evenly spaced and fits on one page. The cover page is mostly empty but looks intentional. A uses a compact Times look with a tight table and an unevenly broken reference list. A also runs the title and abstract together on one page, and its last page is almost empty. B's last page is also nearly empty, with only footnotes on it.

A has a full-bleed illustrated cover with a title band (A1) and bold numbered headings that give clear hierarchy. Its stats row sits directly under the 'What changed' text (A2), and the table is clean (A4). B puts a header band on the first page without a real cover, and its stats row is split from its intro paragraph across the page break (B1 to B2). B also has hyphenation in justified text, thin light headings, and a caption separated from the image by a text block (B2). A's weaknesses are the orphaned caption at the top of A4 and the large empty space on A4, but B has similar empty space on B3.

B puts the title band and authors on the first page with the abstract, so the document starts immediately. A spends a full page on a mostly empty dark cover. B's sans-serif text is clear, and its running header with section names helps navigation. A's serif body has inconsistent sizes: the abstract and Participants text are larger than the Introduction text, which breaks rhythm. Both share the orphaned equation, the "$s_p$" glitch and a nearly empty last page. B splits the equation from its lead-in across pages, but A has a similar weakness.
